title: Temporal co-change calibration, source-boundary exposure vs historical baselines
status: preseal; retrospective author-only calibration, not F38

train.selection: latest 50 API commits at cutoff, then exclude merges; no replenishment

test.selection: oldest 50 from complete paginated interval (committer date ascending, SHA tiebreak), then exclude merges; no replenishment

source: tree of most recent commit before cutoff; fixed universe src/click/*.py (direct children), no test paths; derive direct import graph and imported identifier use in each module using Python AST; separate directional symbol count and unweighted edge; if AST cannot execute locally, use declared restricted text parser and label accordingly, do not substitute silently
outcome: One anchor touched file given, predict other touched files in same commit, restricted to fixed universe; exclude <2 matched paths; rename old and new path if both known; no future fit. Commit-weighted mean across anchors; tie-aware expected reciprocal rank of first hit and pairwise AUC; top-1 tie probability optional.
baselines: historical pair co-change (Jaccard or conditional frequency, ties via marginal frequency)
history + exposure rank fusion equal weights (fixed, no tuning)
controls: Only commit metadata touched paths; no issue interpretation or protected contracts. Source path universe fixed before holdout. If fewer than five held-out eligible commits report insufficiency, do not backfill or change cutoff. Record attrition, source parser, raw metadata, exact selection, comparison by commit and no claim of causal costs.
predictions: Exposure may rank co-changes better than binary import edge when different source edges have different use intensity; historical pair baseline may dominate. Negative result retained.
No evidence of contract-specific advantage from import exposure alone; use as classical baseline for later actual contract features.
scope: Public historical calibration, not independent demand prediction, source contracts, actual workload frequency, labor or structural law; no source modification upstream.
